name: ABBA
hook: A Swedish group who won Eurovision in 1974, built a dense layered studio sound in Stockholm, and almost never let anyone sample them, until Madonna sent a letter.
blurb: ABBA formed in Stockholm in 1972. Its four members were two couples: Agnetha Fältskog and Björn Ulvaeus, and Benny Andersson and Anni-Frid Lyngstad. Björn and Benny wrote the songs, and Stig Anderson was their manager and owned their label, Polar Music. On 6 April 1974, in Brighton, they won the Eurovision Song Contest with 'Waterloo', sung in English, and became one of the best-selling groups ever. Their engineer, Michael B. Tretow, stacked up many recordings of the same parts to make a huge, layered sound that became their signature, and by 1978 they had turned an old Stockholm cinema into their own studio, Polar Music Studio. Both couples divorced during the group's later years, and several of the late songs are often heard as being about that. They stopped in December 1982. Björn and Benny are known for almost never allowing other musicians to sample their songs, which is what makes Madonna's 'Hung Up' (2005) unusual: she sent a letter to Stockholm asking to use 'Gimme! Gimme! Gimme!', and they said yes after negotiating a large share of the royalties. They came back with a new album, 'Voyage', in November 2021, and since May 2022 digital avatars of them have performed the 'ABBA Voyage' concerts in London.
